# PARITY CDP1 — WHAT A SECOND CDP CLIENT ON ONE PAGE TARGET SEES.
#
# RECORDED from google-chrome 150.0.7871.46 on 2026-09-21, headless=new, launched by us with
# `--remote-debugging-port=0 --user-data-dir=<fresh> --no-first-run --no-default-browser-check
# --disable-gpu about:blank` — NOT by Playwright's `launch()`, which adds `--enable-automation`
# (PARITY M1). Two runs, byte-identical.
#
# THE EXPERIMENT. One page target. Client A attaches, navigates to the fixture below, sets one
# global, reads the table, and DETACHES. Client B then attaches to the same target, never
# navigates, and reads the same table. `<BASE>` stands for the loopback origin the fixture was
# served from (`http://127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>`), so the recording does not pin a port.
#
#   <BASE>/fixture.html:
#     <!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8">
#     <title>CDP1 loopback fixture</title></head><body>
#     <h1 id="h">CDP1</h1><p class="p">one page, two clients</p>
#     <div id="d"><span>a</span><span>b</span></div>
#     <script>window.__fixture_ran = true;</script></body></html>
#
# HOW TO READ IT. A line with no prefix is ASSERTED against this engine, line for line. A line
# prefixed `!` is RECORDED AND NOT ASSERTED, and carries the reason on the line; the test counts
# those and fails if the count moves, so nobody can quietly make this file softer. A line that
# differs is a finding about the engine, never a reason to edit this file.
#
# Re-record: tools are in this test's header.

# ── client A: the first client, after navigating to the fixture ──────────────────────────────────
A document.documentElement.tagName = "HTML"
A proto-of-document ctor name = "HTMLDocument"
A String(document) = "[object HTMLDocument]"
A document.readyState = "complete"
A document.title = "CDP1 loopback fixture"
A document.querySelectorAll('*').length = 11
A location.href = "<BASE>/fixture.html"
A window === self = true
A globalThis === window = true
A document === window.document = true
A marker the FIRST client set = "set-by-the-first-client"
A contexts announced = 2
A last context origin = "<BASE>"
A last context isDefault = true

# ── client B: a SECOND client, attached to the same target after A detached; it never navigates ──
#
# Every row below equals A's. That is the whole finding: in Chrome a target IS a page and a client
# is a view onto it, so what the second client reads is what the first one left. korvus answered
# `{"readyState":"complete"}` / prototype `Object` / no `documentElement` / `about:blank` here, on
# `example.com` as well as on this fixture, because it built the second client a whole new realm.
B document.documentElement.tagName = "HTML"
B proto-of-document ctor name = "HTMLDocument"
B String(document) = "[object HTMLDocument]"
B document.readyState = "complete"
B document.title = "CDP1 loopback fixture"
B document.querySelectorAll('*').length = 11
B location.href = "<BASE>/fixture.html"
B window === self = true
B globalThis === window = true
B document === window.document = true
B marker the FIRST client set = "set-by-the-first-client"

# B is announced ONE context — the live one — not the target's history: `Runtime.enable` replays
# the contexts that exist, and the initial `about:blank` context was destroyed by the navigation.
B contexts announced = 1
B last context origin = "<BASE>"
B last context isDefault = true

# THE IDENTITY ROWS, which are what "the same realm" means on this wire. Chrome hands B the same
# execution context object A had: the same id and the same `uniqueId`. They are asserted as the
# EQUALITY rather than as the number, because the number is the next line down and is not ours.
B last context id == A last context id = true
B context uniqueId == A's = true
B frameTree url = "<BASE>/fixture.html"

# ── recorded, NOT asserted ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# The absolute execution-context NUMBER for a post-navigation document. Chrome allocates
# sequentially (1 = the initial about:blank, 2 = the first navigation's document); this server
# reserves 2 for `Page.createIsolatedWorld`'s utility world and numbers the post-navigation
# document 3 (`src/ids.rs::ConnIds::default_context`). It is a difference on the wire and it is
# NOT this lane's: nothing here changes it, and the rows above assert the property that CDP1 is
# about — that both clients are given the SAME context — without depending on which number it is.
! A last context id = 2      # korvus: 3, by the utility-world reservation in src/ids.rs
! B last context id = 2      # korvus: 3, and equal to A's, which is the row that is asserted
